ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the ski jumper starts from rest at point A on the slide and, after a time $t_{0}$, flies off the platform at point O in a horizontal direction. It is known that point $O$ is the starting point of the slope, the vertical distance between point $A$ and point $O$ is $h$, the inclination angle of the slope is $\theta$, the mass of the athlete is $m$, and the acceleration due to gravity is $g$. Friction and air resistance are negligible.

1. The speed $v$ of the athlete when passing the platform $O$.
2. During the motion from point $A$ to point $O$, the average power $\overline{{P_{G}}}$ of the work done by gravity on the athlete.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point A is located at the starting point of the slideway in the upper left, and the athlete starts from A; the slideway curves downward and connects to a lower horizontal platform, with point O marked near the end of the platform. The vertical height difference from A to the horizontal plane where O is located is indicated with a dashed line and labeled h. After point O there is a slope inclined downward to the right, and the angle between the slope and the horizontal plane is labeled θ; this slope is after O and does not affect the energy calculation from A to O. Reasoning: The athlete starts from rest at point A, and friction and air resistance are ignored, so mechanical energy is conserved from A to O. The decrease in gravitational potential energy from A to O is mgh, all converted into the kinetic energy at point O: mgh = (1/2)mv^2. Therefore v = sqrt(2gh). During the process from A to O, the work done by gravity equals the decrease in gravitational potential energy, namely W_G = mgh. The elapsed time is t0, so the average power of the work done by gravity is \overline{P_G} = W_G/t0 = mgh/t0.
